name: General factories and workshops (made-to-order and made-to-stock)

problems.words: Order was promised in two weeks, it's week four and I don't know which stage it's stuck at
quick_ideas: Walk the floor once and write every open order with its promised date and current stage on one board, so you see what is already late
Check what is queued at your slowest stage before giving the next delivery date, so the promise matches what the floor can do

workzap_build.text: A phone job card for every order where the supervisor taps each stage done, with an automatic morning WhatsApp list of open orders, promised dates and days late.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many orders are open right now?
problems.free_stops: The stage list, who taps what and how lateness is flagged are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each open order's current stage with the promised stage by now, so you can spot where late work is stacking up.
Make one line supervisor update a single open-order board at shift end, so everyone checks the same status before giving dates.

problems.words: Job cards go missing between cutting and assembly
quick_ideas: Trace the last few lost cards back to the hand-over where they disappeared, so you know which stage to fix
Give each stage one fixed rack where the card must sit with the batch, so cards stop travelling in pockets

workzap_build.text: Digital job cards that move from stage to stage on supervisors' phones, so no order depends on a paper slip surviving the floor.

problems.ask_first: Which stage hands over most often without the card?
problems.free_stops: How hand-overs are confirmed and who sees a stalled card is covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many job cards reach assembly without the batch during this week, so you know how often the handover is failing.
Make cutting place every finished batch and card on one marked handover shelf, so assembly always checks the same spot.

problems.words: We stopped the line because one raw material ran out and nobody told purchase
quick_ideas: List the handful of materials that can stop production and agree a minimum level for each with the store keeper, so everyone knows the danger line
Check this week's open orders against those items once, so a big order does not quietly drain stock

workzap_build.text: A raw material register with minimum levels that alerts purchase and the owner automatically the moment any item falls below, every day.

problems.ask_first: Which material runs short most often?
problems.free_stops: How minimum levels are worked out per item and who gets which alert sits in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many times this week purchase hears about a low raw material only after production stops, so the handoff delay shows.
Give the store keeper one notebook page for low stock alerts at shift end, so purchase gets a steady signal before lines stop.

problems.words: The store says we have 200 pieces, physically there are 140
quick_ideas: Do one physical count of your fast-moving items and compare with the books, so you see how big the gap really is
Mark separate areas for raw material, work in progress and finished goods, so counts stop getting mixed

workzap_build.text: A store register on phone recording every receipt and issue against a job, with regular counts and photos that flag any difference from the books automatically.

problems.ask_first: Where does the count go wrong most — raw material, work in progress or finished goods?
problems.free_stops: The counting routine, issue rules and how differences are flagged are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count one item from store records to shelf by location this week, so you see where pieces are disappearing or shifting.
Make one store keeper keep all stock corrections in one notebook beside the shelves, so count changes stop getting scattered.

problems.words: I quote a price but don't really know my cost per piece
quick_ideas: Work out the material, labour and machine time in one piece of your best-selling product, so you have one real cost to compare with your price
Check which running quotes still use old supplier rates, so you know where margin is slipping now

workzap_build.text: A bill of materials per product that keeps cost per piece current as supplier rates change and feeds every new quote automatically.

problems.ask_first: How do you work out a price when you quote today?
problems.free_stops: How labour, machine time and overheads are built into the cost is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write one recent job's material used, hours spent and scrap left over, so your quoted piece price has a real floor check.
Make one estimator keep every current cost note in one notebook, so new quotes use the same basis each time.

problems.words: Dealers take months to pay and some never clear the last bill
quick_ideas: Make one list of every dealer with what they owe and since when, so you know who to chase first
Look at each dealer's oldest unpaid bill before the next dispatch, so credit stops growing unnoticed

workzap_build.text: A receivables tracker per dealer with ageing of each bill and polite WhatsApp reminders that go out on schedule without anyone remembering.

problems.ask_first: Is anyone following up on overdue bills today?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing, credit limits and how balances are confirmed with dealers are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare what each dealer still owes with the date of their latest dispatch, so slow payers stand out before more goods go.
Make the accounts clerk review one overdue list at the same time each week, so follow-up stops slipping behind dispatch work.

problems.words: Machine breaks down and we wait days for the mechanic or part
quick_ideas: Write down the last few breakdowns you remember with machine, days lost and part needed, so the worst machines become obvious
Find a second mechanic or workshop you could call, so one person's delay does not stop the floor

workzap_build.text: A machine log on phone for every breakdown, its duration, cause and part, with an automatic monthly list of the machines that stop the most.

problems.free_stops: Which spares to hold and how a maintenance schedule is set per machine are covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which machine waited longest for a mechanic or part this month, so you can see where delays hurt the floor most.
Make one operator leave every machine stoppage note in one fixed place, so the mechanic gets the same handover each time.

problems.words: Customer rejected a whole lot after delivery
quick_ideas: Put one person on a check before packing for the faults customers raise most, so problems are caught inside the gate
Photograph a sample of the next lot before dispatch, so you have a record if a dispute starts

workzap_build.text: A pre-dispatch quality check on phone with photos and rejection reasons per stage, recorded for every lot and summarised for the owner.

problems.ask_first: Is anyone checking goods before dispatch now?
problems.free_stops: The checklist itself and how rejections are traced to a stage are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many pieces from the last rejected lot had the same fault, so you know whether one issue spoiled the shipment.
Make one packer check finished goods against the customer's known complaint point before dispatch, so the same rejection reason is less likely.

problems.words: Orders come on WhatsApp, calls and email and some get forgotten
quick_ideas: Gather every open order from all channels into one list once, so you see what is waiting
Make one person the owner of that list, so orders stop falling between people

workzap_build.text: One order book where WhatsApp, phone and email orders land, each linked to a job card and tracked to dispatch automatically.

problems.free_stops: How orders flow from each channel into production is mapped in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count open orders from calls, messages and email against what reached production, so you see where orders are dropping out.
Make the sales coordinator write every new order in one notebook before sharing it onward, so nothing waits in separate channels.

problems.words: Scrap and offcuts are sold by the floor staff and I never see the money
quick_ideas: Weigh this week's scrap yourself before it leaves the gate, so you have a real figure to compare
Route scrap sales through the office only, so the money arrives in one place

workzap_build.text: A scrap register where every weighing and sale is matched to a receipt, with a monthly comparison against production.

problems.free_stops: Where weighing happens and how weights are matched to sales is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each scrap pile by material and approximate size before it leaves this week, so missing sale money has something concrete behind it.
Make the shift supervisor record every scrap handover in one notebook at dispatch, so floor sales cannot pass without a visible trail.

never_say: Any guarantee of delivery dates, output or fewer breakdowns.
Anything on machine guarding, electrical, boiler or fire safety, or how to "get through" an inspection.
Any interpretation of labour law, minimum wage, contractor liability, EOBI, WPS or CPP/EI; suggest talking to a lawyer or accountant.
Tax, customs or financing advice, or any help with fake invoices, under-invoicing or two sets of books.
Any request for worker names, IDs, phone numbers or bank details; always use roles such as "line supervisor".
Any help optimising child labour or forced overtime.

sample_reply.person: Bhai koi hal batao, orders ka hisaab hi nahi rehta, job card gum ho jate hain aur customer ke phone pe pata chalta hai maal tayyar nahi hua.
sample_reply.pi: Ji bilkul, iska hal mumkin hai aur shuruaat isi hafte ho sakti hai. 1) Ek dafa floor pe ja kar har khula order, wada kiya hua din aur abhi ki stage ek board pe likh dein, taa ke saaf dikhe kaun se order pehle se late hain. 2) Pichle gum hue job cards ko dekh kar woh stage pehchanein jahan card gum hota hai, taa ke usi jagah ko theek kiya ja sake. Workzap yeh kaam aap ke liye khud-ba-khud kar sakta hai: phone pe digital job card jahan supervisor har stage tap kare, aur har subah aap ko WhatsApp pe late orders ki list apne aap mil jaye. Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
